{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./all_to_all_32.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from LSF:
#   -nnodes 32  -> -N 32
#   -W 00:15    -> -t 15m
# jsrun uses: -n32 (resource sets) and -g4 per RS => total GPUs = 32*4 = 128
# jsrun uses: -c40 per RS => request -c 40 (cores per task) for 32 tasks
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 32 -n 32 -c 40 -g 128 -t 15m --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  # NOTE: LSF -J all_to_all_32 not translated.
  # Performance/ops implication: job identification may be less convenient; runtime performance is unaffected.

  # NOTE: LSF -o/-e used %J expansion (jobid) which Flux does not provide portably.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: logs may overwrite unless you generate unique filenames.

  module load gcc
  module load cuda/10.2.89
  module load hwloc

  cd /g/g14/bienz1/BenchPress/spectrum_build/examples || exit 1

  # Start CUDA MPS (node-local)
  nvidia-cuda-mps-control -d

  # Keep jsrun since this is intended for an IBM/Summit-like environment.
  # Run within the allocation.
  flux run -n 32 -c 40 -g 128 \
    jsrun -a40 -c40 -g4 -r1 -n32 -M "-gpu" --latency_priority=gpu-cpu --launch_distribution=packed ./time_alltoall

  echo quit | nvidia-cuda-mps-control
fi
"
}
